Q: Visual Studio does no longer show any devices for my .NET MAUI projects A:

I found a solution to this problem. It's in the version of the .net.
Close your solution and open the .csproj file. At the top, you see:
<TargetFrameworks>net10.0-android etc.. Replace all net10.0 with net9.0 in this line.
Also in the line below: <TargetFrameworks Condition="$([MSBuild]::"... Change the .net10.0 to .net9.0. You can leave the Windows-part as is..
Save your file and open your project and you will see your Android or IOS device again..

Q: Cannot implicitly convert type 'System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnsMode' A:

DataGridViewColumn.AutoSizeMode property expects the value with DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnMode type.

Use the value of DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnsMode type to assign to DataGridView.AutoSizeColumnsMode property.

Q: Error " You dont have permission to attach files to this post" on Wordpress A:

Problem

In WordPress, uploading an image inside the post editor produced:

Sorry, you are not allowed to attach files to this post.

and sometimes:

The link you followed has expired.

Uploading via Media → Add New worked, but the image would not attach to the post.

In the browser network inspector, the upload request to async-upload.php did not include:

post_id
action=upload-attachment

Additionally, post IDs looked like:

9209456194998817742

instead of normal WordPress IDs.

Cause

The site was migrated from Blogger using a WXR file.
The exported XML contained Blogger post IDs (very large 19-digit numbers):

<wp:post_id>9209456194998817742</wp:post_id>

WordPress expects normal incremental integers for post IDs.
Using these very large IDs caused the media uploader permission check (current_user_can('edit_post', $post_id)) to fail, preventing attachments from linking to posts.

Solution

Edit the WXR file before importing so WordPress can generate proper IDs.

Replace all Blogger IDs with 0.

Example replacement:

Find:

<wp:post_id>\d+</wp:post_id>

Replace with:

<wp:post_id>0</wp:post_id>

In Notepad++:

  1. Press Ctrl + H

  2. Search mode → Regular expression

Find:

<wp:post_id>\s*\d+\s*</wp:post_id>

Replace:

<wp:post_id>0</wp:post_id>

Then reset posts before importing:

TRUNCATE TABLE wp_posts;
TRUNCATE TABLE wp_postmeta;
ALTER TABLE wp_posts AUTO_INCREMENT = 1;

Re-import the WXR file.

WordPress will assign normal IDs like:

1
2
3
...

After this, the media uploader correctly sends:

post_id=123
action=upload-attachment

and images attach to posts normally.

Q: parse json file to Pydantic model A:

The data in your example.json doesn't seem to cause all of the errors, only some.

Here's why:

In your SkipDTO, for example, you are defining a no_valid: int field.

With this definition, that field is required, which is why it cannot be null/None.

However, you are passing in:

...
"skips": [
{
        "valid": null,
        "no_valid": null,
        "attestation_start_date": "2020-03-09",
        "attestation_end_date": "2020-03-14"
    }
]
...

If null is a valid value for no_valid (and valid) then you need to adapt your model to the following:

from typing import List, Dict, Optional

class SkipDTO(OurBaseModel):
    valid: Optional[int]
    no_valid: Optional[int]
    attestation_start_date: date

An Optional field will be set to None if a null value is passed in.

The same is probably the case for AttestationDTO.value and maybe other fields in your models.
